display.purpose: Largest type in the product. Dialog and page titles only; appears twice in the entire stylesheet.

title.purpose: Home-feed section headings such as 'Recommended for you'.

body.purpose: Navigation items, chips, search input, general interface copy.

label.purpose: Uppercase section eyebrows and field labels, always in Deep Smoke. The only uppercase in the system.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dropdown menus and popovers. The --shadow token.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs only; must separate from a whole page rather than a local panel.

shadows.name: thumbnail-lift
shadows.purpose: Under overlaid thumbnail badges so duration text survives a light frame behind it.

shadows.name: status-glow-healthy
shadows.purpose: Halo under a healthy playback-source dot. Diagnostic only.

shadows.name: status-glow-cooling
shadows.purpose: Halo under a source in cooldown.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The only focus treatment in the system. Never colored.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Default for background and color state changes. The most common transition in the stylesheet.

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: Pill and button state changes, including border materialization.

motion.name: move
motion.purpose: Transform and opacity changes on larger moving elements.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The scale(.96) active-press curve. The system's signature feedback.

motion.name: press-overshoot
motion.purpose: Slight-overshoot variant used on one reaction control.

narrative.overview:
OpenFeed looks like an instrument panel running in a dark room. The interface sits at near-black and stays there; nothing glows, nothing gradients, nothing competes with the thumbnails. Every surface is one of four steps on a single cold-grey ramp, separated by hairlines thin enough to read as seams rather than boxes. The result is a shell that disappears the moment content loads into it — which is the point, because the content is video artwork and the chrome's job is to hold it without arguing.

Density is deliberate and high. Type runs small (11–17px across almost the entire interface) and lands on half-pixel steps — 11.5, 12.5, 13.5, 14.5 — because the system would rather fit one more row of real information than pad a card. Weights do the same thing at finer grain than usual, using 550, 650, and 680 where most systems would jump 500 → 600 → 700. This is a tool for someone who uses it every day and already knows where everything is, so legibility beats spaciousness and scanability beats emphasis.

Color is treated as instrumentation, not decoration. The palette is functionally monochrome, and the red is a light on a panel: it marks the brand, unread activity, danger, and failure, and it stays off the rest of the time. A blue appears only where a human wrote a link. A green and an amber appear only where a backend is reporting its own health. Nothing in the system is colored because color would look nice there.
keyCharacteristics: Four-step tonal ramp from #0a0a0b to #232327; depth from value, not shadow
Hairline borders at 5.5–9% white; no heavy strokes anywhere
Pill-first geometry — 52 of 144 radius declarations are fully round
Small, dense type on half-pixel steps with intermediate weights (550/650/680)
Accent red used 33 times across 1,371 lines of CSS, almost all of it status
Press feedback is physical: controls scale to 96% on :active

rules.name: The Panel Light Rule
rules.body: Ember means something happened here or this will destroy something. It is never a decorative fill, never a default button background, and never an active-state background. One exception is permitted: a single filled Ember primary action per screen, and only where the user is making a real commitment (deleting data, wiping history, confirming an irreversible import). If two red fills appear on one screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Read-It-Don't-See-It Rule
rules.body: When red must be read as text, use Ember Text (#f2686c), not Ember. Ember is for shapes you notice; Ember Text is for words you read.

rules.name: The Borrowed Blue Rule
rules.body: Cobalt Link belongs to creator-authored content. Product chrome never uses it — a blue button would read as someone else's link.

rules.name: The Half-Step Rule
rules.body: The scale moves in half-pixels (11.5, 12.5, 13.5, 14.5) on purpose. When a new size is needed, take the nearest existing step rather than introducing a round number — a 14px title next to a 14.5px one reads as a mistake, not a variation.

rules.name: The Uppercase Tax Rule
rules.body: Uppercase appears only at 11px/600 with +0.07em tracking, and only for eyebrows and field labels. Uppercase at any other size is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Ramp-Not-Riser Rule
rules.body: To make something feel raised, move it up the tonal ramp (Graphite → Dry Slate) and let its hairline do the separating. Reach for box-shadow only when the element genuinely overlaps unrelated content — a menu, a dialog. A shadow on an in-flow card is out of system.

dos: Do move up the tonal ramp for emphasis — Graphite at rest, Dry Slate on hover — and let the 1px hairline do the containing.
Do reach for 999px first. If a new control is not a container, it is probably a pill.

Do carry the scale(.96) press onto any new pressable control, paired with a prefers-reduced-motion guard that disables both the transition and the transform. The stylesheet already has nine such guards; match the pattern.
Do use Ember Text (#f2686c) whenever red needs to be read as words.
Do keep new type on the existing half-pixel steps (11, 11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14.5, 17, 19) and the existing weights (500, 550, 600, 650).
Do invert — Bone background, Blackout text — to mark a selected filter.
Do put status color only where a backend is actually reporting status.
donts: Don't use Ember as a background fill for an ordinary control, an active tab, or a selected chip. The system marks those with tonal shift and inversion. The single permitted exception is one filled Ember confirm action per screen, on a genuinely destructive commitment.
Don't add box-shadow to anything that sits in normal flow. Shadows are for menus and dialogs.
Don't introduce a second font family. The system is one platform-native stack tuned by weight and tracking.
Don't use Cobalt Link (#6ea8ff) in product chrome — it means 'a creator wrote this.'
Don't put borders wider than 1px, or borders in any color other than white at low alpha, in a resting state.
Don't give video cards a fill, a border, or padding. The thumbnail is the container.
Don't assume an 8pt grid. Spacing here is 2px-granular, and 6px/10px/14px are first-class values.
Don't add a colored focus ring. Focus is always 0 0 0 2px rgba(255,255,255,.3).
